subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the main benefit of using a layered model (such as TCP/IP) for networking?
options: It removes the need for any protocols
It guarantees no data is ever lost
It makes networks slower but cheaper
It breaks communication into self-contained layers that can be developed and changed independently
questions.explain: Layering splits networking into independent self-contained tasks, so each layer can be developed or changed without affecting the others.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of DNS on the internet?
options: To translate domain names into IP addresses
To store website files
To encrypt web traffic
To assign physical MAC addresses
questions.explain: DNS translates human-readable domain names into the IP addresses computers use.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a firewall?
options: To physically clean dust from a server
To translate domain names to IP addresses
To monitor and control incoming and outgoing network traffic
To increase the network bandwidth
questions.explain: A firewall monitors and controls network traffic based on security rules.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of encrypting data sent across a network?
options: To speed up the connection
To scramble it so that it is meaningless to anyone who intercepts it without the key
To convert it into a MAC address
To compress it so it takes less space
questions.explain: Encryption scrambles data so that an interceptor without the decryption key cannot understand it.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of social engineering?
options: Pretending to be IT support over the phone to persuade a worker to reveal their password
Splitting data into packets for transmission
Encrypting files with a strong key
Flooding a server with automated traffic
questions.explain: Social engineering manipulates people into giving away information, such as impersonating IT support to obtain a password.

questions.q: What is the role of a router in a network?
options: To physically connect a device to the network cable
To convert digital signals to analogue only
To boost a signal along a single cable
To direct data packets between different networks
questions.explain: A router directs (routes) data packets between different networks.

questions.q: Which protocol is primarily used to send email between mail servers?
options: HTTP
SMTP
DNS
FTP
questions.explain: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send email between servers.

questions.q: An attacker enters malicious database commands into a website's input box to access its data. This is called:
options: Social engineering
Phishing
A man-in-the-middle attack
SQL injection
questions.explain: SQL injection enters malicious SQL commands through an input field to manipulate or access a database.

questions.q: How do an IP address and a MAC address differ?
options: An IP address is permanent while a MAC address changes each session
Only MAC addresses are used on the internet
An IP address can change between networks while a MAC address is fixed to the hardware
They are two names for exactly the same thing
questions.explain: An IP address can change depending on the network, whereas a MAC address is fixed to the device's hardware.

questions.q: Which protocol is used to securely transfer web pages?
options: SMTP
FTP
HTTPS
POP3
questions.explain: HTTPS is the secure (encrypted) version of HTTP used to transfer web pages.

questions.q: A brute force attack works by:
options: Overloading a server with traffic
Reading data sent over an unencrypted connection
Tricking a user with a fake website
Systematically trying many possible passwords until one works
questions.explain: A brute force attack tries many password combinations until the correct one is found.

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares a wired and a wireless connection?
options: Wired connections cannot transfer data at all
Wireless connections are always faster and more reliable than wired
Wired connections are generally faster and more reliable but less convenient than wireless
Wireless connections never suffer from interference
questions.explain: Wired (e.g. Ethernet) connections are usually faster and more reliable, while wireless trades some speed/reliability for greater convenience.

questions.q: What is a key advantage of a mesh topology over a star topology?
options: There is no single point of failure as data can take multiple routes
It requires a central switch
It is always cheaper to install
It uses less cabling
questions.explain: A mesh provides multiple paths between devices, so there is no single point of failure.

questions.q: What is a MAC address?
options: A unique physical address permanently assigned to a network interface card
The amount of data a network can carry
A temporary address assigned by a router each time you connect
A human-readable name for a website
questions.explain: A MAC address is a unique, permanent (physical) identifier assigned to a device's network interface card.

questions.q: Which statement about a peer-to-peer network is correct?
options: A central server controls all the data
It always requires specialist server software
Clients cannot share files with one another
All computers have equal status and can share resources directly
questions.explain: In peer-to-peer networks all computers have equal status and share resources directly.

questions.q: In a star network topology, how are devices connected?
options: Every device connects to a central switch or hub
Devices share a single backbone cable
Each device connects directly to every other device
Devices are connected in a single closed loop
questions.explain: In a star topology every device connects to a central switch or hub.

questions.q: Which attack involves tricking people into revealing confidential information, e.g. via fake emails?
options: SQL injection
Brute force attack
Denial of service
Phishing
questions.explain: Phishing tricks people into revealing confidential information, often using fake emails.

questions.q: What is the main aim of a Denial of Service (DoS) attack?
options: To steal a database of passwords
To insert malicious SQL into a database
To flood a server with requests so it cannot respond to legitimate users
To physically damage network cables
questions.explain: A DoS attack floods a server with traffic so it cannot serve legitimate users.

questions.q: In a client-server network, what does the server typically do?
options: Provides shared resources and services to clients
Cannot control access to files
Relies on each client to store all the data
Has equal status with every other computer
questions.explain: In client-server, the server provides centralised resources and services to clients.

questions.q: What does the bandwidth of a network refer to?
options: The physical length of the cabling
The number of devices connected
The amount of data that can be transmitted in a given time
The distance between two routers
questions.explain: Bandwidth is the amount of data that can be transmitted in a given time.

questions.q: Which best describes a LAN?
options: A network that only uses wireless connections
A network covering a large geographical area such as a country
A network connecting devices across different continents
A network covering a small geographical area such as a single site or building
questions.explain: A LAN (Local Area Network) covers a small geographical area, typically one site or building.

questions.q: What does a NIC (Network Interface Card) do?
options: Allows a device to connect to a network
Allocates IP addresses to all devices
Encrypts all outgoing data
Translates domain names to IP addresses
questions.explain: A NIC allows a device to physically connect to and communicate on a network.
